entries.title: Ezekiel 7:1
segments:
vv 1-13. 
 
God bears long with sinners, "not willing that any should perish, but that all should come to repentance;" yet if they persist in disregarding his warnings, he will execute upon them all his threatened judgments without mitigation.

entries.title: Ezekiel 7:4
segments: Thine abominations shall be; that is, the recompense of thine abominations shall come.

entries.title: Ezekiel 7:6
segments: Watcheth for thee; or waketh up against thee, as an enemy intent on thy destruction.

entries.title: Ezekiel 7:7
segments: The morning; the morning of the day of trouble.  So also

. 
 
  Not the sounding again of the mountains; the resounding of the mountains with joyous shouts.  It is a cry of trouble, and not of gladness.

entries.title: Ezekiel 7:10
segments: Pride hath budded; into a rod.  The pride and violence of the people have grown into a rod which Jehovah will use to punish their wickedness.  Compare

entries.title: Ezekiel 7:12
segments: Buyer rejoice--seller mourn; because in the approaching day of captivity buyer and seller will be alike poor and miserable.

entries.title: Ezekiel 7:13
segments: Return to that which is sold; return at the year of the jubilee to the possession of his inheritance which he has sold.

Although they were yet alive; although the sellers were yet alive at the year of jubilee; for the land shall be in the possession of the enemy.  This is added to make the picture of the desolation of the land complete. 
 
  Is touching the whole multitude thereof; threatens not a partial, but a universal devastation of the land.

entries.title: Ezekiel 7:14
segments:
They have blown the trumpet; the Jewish leaders, to summon the people to battle against their enemies. 
 
  None goeth to the battle; God's wrath has taken from the people all their courage.
When God will destroy a people for their iniquity, he takes from them courage and counsel in the day of trouble, and gives them up to terror and confusion.

entries.title: Ezekiel 7:16
segments: Like doves of the valleys; with allusion to the mourning noise of doves.

entries.title: Ezekiel 7:19
segments:
Cast their silver in the streets; in their flight. 
 
  Shall be removed; or, "shall become an unclean thing;" that is, be cast away as an unclean thing. 
 
  Satisfy their souls; with their wealth.  God's judgments shall reduce rich and poor to a common level. 
 
The wealth of wicked men is no protection against God's judgments. With infinite ease he can destroy them and their possessions together.

entries.title: Ezekiel 7:20
segments:
The beauty of his ornament; the temple, or the land of Palestine, which was "the glory of all lands." 
 
  He set it; God set it. 
 
  Set it far from them; or, "made it to them an unclean thing." Compare

entries.title: Ezekiel 7:22
segments:
From them; from my people. 
 
  They shall pollute; the robbers immediately mentioned; that is, foreign enemies. 
 
  My secret place; my sanctuary. 
 
vv 22-25. 
 
God would not spare his ancient people when they sinned against him, on account of their "holy and beautiful temple," with its divinely appointed ordinances; neither will he spare unfaithful churches now, on account of their outward relations and privileges.

entries.title: Ezekiel 7:23
segments: Make a chain; or binding the rebellious Jews and leading them into captivity.

entries.title: Ezekiel 7:26
segments: They who will not listen when God graciously calls them to repentance and obedience, shall call upon him in the time of trouble, but receive no answer.
